definitions.explanation: Leave from work granted to a woman before and after childbirth. In Japan, legally mandated as 6 weeks before the due date and 8 weeks after birth.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}から{産休|さんきゅう}に{入|はい}ります。
examples.english: I'll be going on maternity leave starting next month.

examples.japanese: {産休|さんきゅう}から{復帰|ふっき}したばかりです。
examples.english: I just returned from maternity leave.

examples.japanese: {産休|さんきゅう}・{育休|いくきゅう}を{取|と}る{社員|しゃいん}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More employees are taking maternity and parental leave.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
Abbreviation of {産前産後休業|さんぜんさんごきゅうぎょう} (pre- and post-natal leave).

{産|さん} (childbirth) + {休|きゅう} (leave/rest)

COLLOCATIONS:
・{産休|さんきゅう}に{入|はい}る - to go on maternity leave
・{産休|さんきゅう}を{取|と}る - to take maternity leave
・{産休|さんきゅう}から{復帰|ふっき}する - to return from maternity leave
・{産休|さんきゅう}・{育休|いくきゅう} - maternity and parental leave (often paired)

LEGAL CONTEXT:
Under Japanese labor law, maternity leave ({産前産後休業|さんぜんさんごきゅうぎょう}) consists of:
・{産前|さんぜん}{休業|きゅうぎょう}: 6 weeks before due date (8 weeks for multiple births)
・{産後|さんご}{休業|きゅうぎょう}: 8 weeks after birth (mandatory)

This is distinct from {育児休業|いくじきゅうぎょう} (parental leave), which can follow maternity leave.
